A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E are available and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Transformer experiments on parity, multi-operand addition, and multiplication, together with architectural ablations and attention analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original results on all three tasks and reports additional controlled experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed scratchpads and position-coupling procedures remain unchanged: single-level coupling for parity, bi-level coupling for addition, and the two-stage scratchpad with tri-level coupling for multiplication. New architectural and formatting variants are evaluated as ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic parity, multi-operand addition, and integer multiplication over the same task and length coverage. The new experiments vary model dimensions, dataset sizes, and preprocessing within that retained coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 3 substantially broadens the parity comparison. v1 compares against NoPE with and without scratchpads; v2 additionally evaluates RoPE and FIRE, each with and without scratchpads. The comparator sets for addition and multiplication remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the reported parity learning rate from 0.0001 to 0.00003. New Appendix C experiments introduce controlled head-width comparisons at fixed embedding dimension, embedding-width sweeps, training sizes from 20K to 10M examples, and six input-format configurations. These extend the evaluation design without replacing the default arithmetic setup.

E4.justification: v2 retains the existing training-length, zero-padding, architecture, and attention analyses. Appendix C adds substantial investigations of head width independently of embedding width, embedding-size sensitivity, training-data quantity, and combinations of reversal and zero-padding, presented in v2 Figures 11–14.

E5.justification: Figure 1 reports eight runs for every configuration in v2, versus four for the comparators and six for the proposed configuration in v1. Figure 3 newly identifies its shaded regions as 95% confidence intervals; both versions already report eight-run parity medians.

E6.justification: Figure 3 replaces the parity results: NoPE without scratchpad changes from approximately chance-level in-distribution accuracy to near-perfect accuracy there, under the revised reported learning rate. Figure 1's addition heatmaps also change. New Appendix C results establish head/embedding-width sensitivity, little effect of training-set size, and substantial input-format effects. Figure 9's multiplication results are retained.

T1.justification: Where v1 Appendix D.7.1 merely refers to an external construction, v2 D.6.1 explicitly defines the carry-adjusted function g and ReLU functions for digit prediction, explaining the adaptation to its PRE_CARRY representation. Illustrative entries in Tables 4 and 25 are also corrected. Theorem 4.1 and its dimensional bound remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The headline claims of approximately 2–3× arithmetic length generalization and the one-layer existence theorem remain. The contribution summary makes a limited qualification, replacing v1's claim of attending to only two number tokens per prediction with a constant number of tokens in v2.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds a head-width explanation for the 1L8H versus 1L4H performance gap and distinguishes optimization benefits of larger embeddings from theoretical expressivity. Appendix A.1 introduces an architectural-implementation hypothesis for disagreement with McLeish et al.'s multiplication results. The stated applicability limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents the fixed and varied settings of its new ablations and explains that starting position IDs are fixed arbitrarily at test time. Appendix B removes the explicit Kazemnejad-codebase provenance and upstream URL. The authors' own code link, hardware information, and training-time summaries remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Gehring et al., Qian et al., and Sabbaghi et al., and removes Friedman et al., Lindner et al., and Weiss et al. with the deleted proof-attribution footnote. It also expands the discussion of disagreement with McLeish et al.; the central positioning around scratchpads and Position Coupling remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose revisions, consolidates and reorders background material under Section 2.1, expands selected explanations, and reorganizes residual-connection subsections in Appendix D. The overall argument and main section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout, moves Figure 1 onto the title page, expands Figure 3 to seven series, and adds four multi-panel ablation figures. It also resizes existing displays and places Tables 2 and 3 together. The earlier Appendix E attention figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens specific parts of an already supported paper: Appendix C controls the head-count/head-width confound, the parity comparison includes broader baselines that learn the training distribution, and Appendix D makes the carry computation directly checkable. These targeted gains outweigh the smaller plot displays and removal of upstream-code provenance. The central arithmetic evidence is largely retained, and the new explanation for disagreement with McLeish et al. remains a hypothesis.
